Perform Nested Cross-Validation for Multiple Survival Models

Source: R/machine_learning.R
cross_validation_custom.Rd

This function performs nested cross-validation with hyperparameter tuning across multiple survival models using the tidymodels framework. It supports both standard stratified cross-validation (by event rate) and Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) stratification, which balances by cohort × event combinations.

Usage

cross_validation_custom(
  df_features,
  df_outcome,
  outcome_col,
  event_col,
  ml_options = list(nb_folds = 5, nb_repeats = 1, ncores = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
    LODO = FALSE, batch_id = NULL),
  file_name = NULL
)

Arguments

df_features

A data frame (or tibble) containing predictor variables (X matrix).

df_outcome

A data frame (or tibble) containing survival outcome columns: typically survival time and event indicator.

outcome_col

Character string specifying the name of the survival time column.

event_col

Character string specifying the name of the event indicator column (0 = censored, 1 = event).

ml_options

A named list of machine learning options controlling cross-validation and parallelization:

nb_folds

Number of folds for v-fold cross-validation (default = 5).

nb_repeats

Number of repetitions of cross-validation (default = 1).

ncores

Number of CPU cores for parallel processing (default = parallel::detectCores() - 1).

LODO

Logical; if TRUE, use Leave-One-Domain-Out stratification by cohort × event.

batch_id

Character; name of the cohort or batch column (required if LODO = TRUE).

file_name

Optional character string specifying the file name suffix for saving the generated C-index summary plot (PDF).

Details

For each model and hyperparameter configuration, the function:

  1. Trains the model across multiple folds

  2. Computes the C-index (concordance index)

  3. Aggregates median and MAD (robust variability measure) across folds

Finally, it identifies the best-performing model and hyperparameter configuration and returns all results in a structured list.
